title: Run your first 1:1 with your manager
why_matters: The first 1:1 with your manager is also a calibration on what 'a good SM in this organisation' looks like. SMs are assessed on softer signals than PMs or BAs — trajectory, how the team feels, what's quietly working — and your manager's version of those signals is what you need to learn. Done well, this is the meeting you use throughout your probation to check 'am I reading the room the way she'd read it'.
steps: Book a recurring weekly 30-minute 1:1 if one doesn't exist. Don't wait. SMs without weekly manager time become SMs without trajectory feedback.

Draft a one-page agenda for the first session. Three sections: 'what I'm noticing about this team in week 1' (not yet recommendations — observations); 'questions I have about how things are done here'; 'what would help me from you'.

In the meeting itself, ask the same question every SM probation review will turn on: 'what does a good Scrum Master in this organisation look like — both how you'd describe it now and how you'd describe it in a year?'. The two-horizon version is the SM-specific framing; the answer tells you what trajectory she's looking for.
Listen more than you talk. Most new SMs over-share their plans in the first 1:1; the ones who do well listen for what their manager actually values.
success_criteria: Meeting happened, recurring slot is in both calendars, and you walked out with one concrete sentence on what your manager values most in a Scrum Master beyond 'gets the work done'.
reflection_prompt: Of what your manager said in answer to the 'good SM' question, which part did you not expect? Two sentences.
